Hi Jane — thanks for the quick read and for flagging Helix's concerns. I quoted your key points below and included a concise proposal to get us across the line without reopening the whole MSA.

On Tue, Jan 12, 2027 at 09:02 AM Jane Doe <jane.doe@helixanalytics.com> wrote:
> Our GC has a couple of items that need clarity before we can move to signature: primarily the damages exclusion language. In your MSA redline we see a one-way exclusion for consequential/special/incidental/punitive damages in Redwood's favor and a mutual cap elsewhere — our legal team is uncomfortable with a one-way carve-out.

Proposal (summary) — aim: mutual exclusion but preserve core remedies and carveouts that Helix needs
- Convert the consequential/special/incidental/punitive exclusion to a mutual exclusion (both Parties waive these categories).
- Explicit carveouts (i.e., exceptions to the exclusion) for: (i) gross negligence or willful misconduct, (ii) payment obligations, (iii) indemnifiable third-party IP claims, (iv) liability arising from Redwood's breach of confidentiality and (v) regulatory fines/penalties that cannot be insured away.
- Preserve the negotiated per-claim and aggregate caps elsewhere in the MSA (we propose to keep the existing numeric caps in the Order Form).
- Add a short definitional note: "Consequential damages" expressly includes lost profits and loss of business but excludes direct loss of data where such loss results from Redwood's security failure (that remains a direct claim).

Suggested compromise language (for legal redline):
"Notwithstanding anything to the contrary, neither Party shall be liable to the other for consequential, special, incidental, or punitive damages, except for (a) liability resulting from gross negligence or willful misconduct; (b) either Party's payment obligations; (c) indemnity obligations related to third-party intellectual property infringement; (d) liability arising from a breach of confidentiality obligations; and (e) regulatory fines or penalties imposed on a Party resulting from that Party's non-compliance with applicable law."

If Helix accepts this mutual framing, we think we can preserve the Order Form caps and move to signature today. Rishi and Laura are cc'ed for legal comfort checks — Rishi, Laura: any commercial/legal risk I missed?

Best,
Marissa Cole

Marissa / Jane — quick legal note from my side. I agree with Marissa's compromise framing as a productive middle ground. A few clarifications and minor edits I recommend to reduce ambiguity:

1) Define "Consequential damages" inline to avoid disparate interpretations:
   - "Consequential damages" means indirect or special losses including, but not limited to, lost profits, loss of business, loss of revenue, and loss of anticipated savings.
2) Carveout refinement: replace "regulatory fines or penalties" with "civil monetary fines and penalties actually assessed by a competent governmental authority as a result of a Party's breach or non-compliance" — this narrows scope to fines actually assessed (not mere risk of regulation).
3) Data loss: keep "loss of data" as a direct damage where the loss is caused by Redwood's failure to implement and maintain reasonable security measures — language should track our security appendix.
4) Add an exceptions sentence for third-party claims resulting from Helix's product misuse (so Redwood can't be on the hook for Helix's customers misusing outputs).

Updated redline snippet I propose to insert into Section X (Limitation of Liability):
"Except for obligations expressly set forth in this Agreement (including payment obligations and indemnity provisions), neither Party shall be liable for consequential, special, incidental or punitive damages, as defined herein, except to the extent such damages arise from (i) gross negligence or willful misconduct, (ii) the Party's payment obligations, (iii) indemnity obligations for third-party intellectual property claims, (iv) liability resulting from breach of confidentiality obligations, or (v) civil monetary fines and penalties actually assessed by a competent governmental authority resulting from the Party's breach of law. Notwithstanding the foregoing, direct damages shall include loss of data where such loss is caused by the provider's failure to implement and maintain reasonable security measures in accordance with the Security Addendum."

I will sign off on the language if Helix is comfortable with the narrow regulatory carveout and the data/security qualifier. If Helix prefers broader language on regulatory exposure we will need to route to commercial for cap adjustments.

Rishi
